post.description: To read the full text of a Cornell Chronicle story about Cornell research, people or events, given its news.cornell.edu/stories/... URL (for example from list_stories).

max_chars.description:
Truncate content to this many characters; the full text is returned when omitted.

Provider reference: minimum 200; maximum 2000000.

200.description:
One Cornell Chronicle story as clean Markdown: title, authors, author unit, publication date, Chronicle category, topics, teaser, the body with headings, lists, quotes and inline links, and the list of links in the body. Photos, captions and related-story boxes are left out. max_chars caps the content. Unknown stories are not_found.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authors` | string[] | Named authors; empty for unsigned stories (common before 2015). |
| `byline_unit` | string | Office or unit credited under the byline, e.g. Cornell Research and Innovation; null when absent. |
| `category` | string | Chronicle section label above the headline, e.g. Around Cornell; null when absent. |
| `chars` | number | Characters in the full content before truncation. |
| `content` | string | Story body as Markdown. |
| `links` | object[] | Distinct links in the body, in order. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `published_on` | string | Publication date, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `summary` | string | The page's description (teaser); null when absent. |
| `title` | string |  |
| `topics` | string[] | Topic and campus tags shown under the story. |
| `truncated` | boolean |  |
| `url` | string | Canonical story URL after redirects. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

value.content:
More than 99.9% of peer-reviewed scientific papers agree that climate change is mainly caused by humans, according to a new survey of 88,125 climate-related studies.

The research updates a similar 2013 paper revealing that 97% of studies published between 1991 and 2012 supported the idea that human activities are altering Earth’s climate. The current survey examines the literature published from 2012 to November 2020 to explore whether the consensus has changed.

“We are virtually certain that the consensus is well over 99% now and that it’s pretty much case closed for any meaningful public conversation about the reality of human-caused climate change,” said Mark Lynas, a visiting fellow at the Alliance for Science and the paper’s first author.

“It's critical to acknowledge the principal role of greenhouse gas emissions so that we can rapidly mobilize new solutions, since we are already witnessing in real time the devastating impacts of climate related disasters on businesses, people and the economy,” said Benjamin Houlton, the Ronald P. Lynch Dean of the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and a co-author of the study, “[Greater than 99% Consensus on Human Caused Climate Change in the Peer-Reviewed Scientific Literature](https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1748-9326/ac2966),” which published Oct. 19 in the journal Environmental Research Letters.

In spite of such results, public opinion polls as well as opinions of politicians and public representatives point to false beliefs and claims that a significant debate still exists among scientists over the true cause of climate change. In 2016, the Pew Research Center found that only 27% of U.S. adults believe that “almost all” scientists agreed that climate change is due to human activity, according to the paper. A 2021 Gallup poll pointed to a deepening partisan divide in American politics on whether Earth’s rising observed temperatures since the Industrial Revolution were primarily caused by humans.

“To understand where a consensus exists, you have to be able to quantify it,” Lynas said. “That means surveying the literature in a coherent and non-arbitrary way in order to avoid trading cherry-picked papers, which is often how these arguments are carried out in the public sphere.”

In the study, the researchers began by examining a random sample of 3,000 studies from the dataset of 88,125 English-language climate papers published between 2012 and 2020. They found only found four out of the 3,000 papers were skeptical of human-caused climate change. “We knew that [climate skeptical papers] were vanishingly small in terms of their occurrence, but we thought there still must be more in the 88,000,” Lynas said.

Co-author Simon Perry, a United Kingdom-based software engineer and volunteer at the Alliance for Science, created an algorithm that searched out keywords from papers the team knew were skeptical, such as “solar,” “cosmic rays” and “natural cycles.” The algorithm was applied to all 88,000-plus papers, and the program ordered them so the skeptical ones came higher in the order. They found many of these dissenting papers near the top, as expected, with diminishing returns further down the list. Overall, the search yielded 28 papers that were implicitly or explicitly skeptical, all published in minor journals.

If the 97% result from the 2013 study still left some doubt on scientific consensus on the human influence on climate, the current findings go even further to allay any uncertainty, Lynas said. “This pretty much should be the last word,” he said.

Support for the Alliance for Science is provided by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

post.description: To find recent Cornell research news and announcements, e.g. the latest stories on artificial intelligence, from Weill Cornell Medicine, or about climate, before reading one with get_story.

limit.description:
Stories to return (default 20).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50.

q.description: Case-insensitive text that must appear in the title, teaser, byline or a tag.

topic.description:
Feed to read: all (default), a research topic (artificial-intelligence, law-government-public-policy, ...), a college or school (law-school, engineering, weill-cornell-medicine, ...), a campus section (news-events, inclusion-belonging, ...) or a location (ithaca, doha, ...).

200.description:
Latest Cornell Chronicle stories (up to 50, newest first) from the site's JSON feed for all stories or one topic, college, campus section or location: id, URL, title, teaser, publication time, byline and tags. q filters the feed's rows by title, teaser, byline or tag (case-insensitive). Feeds hold only the 50 most recent stories of their topic; there is no deeper archive or full-text search.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | number |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `q` | string | Normalized filter text; null when absent. |
| `stories` | object[] |  |
| `topic` | string |  |
| `topic_name` | string | Feed name as the feeds page shows it. |
| `total` | number | Feed rows matching q (all rows when q is absent), at most 50. |

stories.summary: Registration is now open for Cornell University’s online Winter Session. Classes run Jan. 4–22, giving students the opportunity to explore an interest, fulfill a requirement, or earn credits before the spring semester.
stories.title: Winter Session 2027 registration is now open

stories.summary: McWhorter, associate professor of linguistics at Columbia University, will offer a talk Nov. 2 as part of the College of Arts & Science's America250 events.
stories.title: John McWhorter to consider ‘Is America a Failed Experiment?’

stories.summary: Funded by a research grant from the Russell Sage Foundation, Brooks faculty members Neil Lewis Jr. and Jeff Niederdeppe will engage in new research to evaluate the effectiveness of race- and class-based messaging strategies targeting racialized policy issues.
tags: Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy
stories.title: Brooks team to research effectiveness of race- and class-based policy communication

stories.summary: Sociologist Holly Jean Buck, Ph.D. ’17, a member of the University at Buffalo faculty, is one of 20 recipients of this year’s MacArthur Fellowships, known as the “genius grants,” for her research on climate change and environmental policy.
stories.title: Sociologist alumna who studies climate change wins MacArthur Fellowship

stories.summary: Esta Bigler, director of Labor Law and Employment Programs at the ILR School, presented on the topic of fair chance hiring at the New York State Bar Association’s Labor and Employment Law Section fall meeting, held in Ithaca earlier this month.
tags: School of Industrial and Labor Relations
stories.title: Bigler shares fair chance hiring best practices with N.Y. lawyers

stories.summary: Cornell University’s “Unmasking the CCP” lecture series will feature talks by former U.S. Ambassador Michael McFaul Oct. 23 and historian Frank Dikötter Oct. 27 on democracy, communism and China’s international role.
stories.title: October lectures explore autocracy, communism and U.S.-China-Russia relations

stories.summary: Private equity firms’ investment in home care agencies perpetuates poor working conditions for workers by continuing the exploitation that is prevalent across the industry, according to a new study from the ILR School’s Worker Institute.
tags: School of Industrial and Labor Relations
stories.title: Private equity ownership results in poor working conditions in NYS home care

stories.summary: A Cornell University Library exhibit, “Weathering the Storm,” which examines the intersection of the environment, labor and workwear, opens Oct. 8 at the ILR School’s Catherwood Library.
tags: School of Industrial and Labor Relations
stories.title: Exhibit weaves together clothing, work and the environment

stories.summary: As an undergraduate researcher, Maya Mangala-Munuma '25 found that trees were three times more likely to be damaged in impoverished, racially diverse neighborhoods.
tags: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
stories.title: More damaged trees mean fewer ecosystem benefits for low-income residents

stories.summary: New York state could catalyze a widespread clean energy transition and address its affordability issues by leveraging one of its most important resources – homes – according to a new report from the Climate Jobs Institute at the ILR School.
tags: School of Industrial and Labor Relations
stories.title: CJI releases "blueprint" to address decarbonization in NY state homes
